name: Street Custom 'Coffin Nail' Lock Bypass Kit
product_name: Street Custom 'Coffin Nail' Lock Bypass Kit
description: A lockpicking and access bypass toolkit assembled from commercially available and custom-fabricated components, contained in a leather roll the size of a pencil case. The kit includes traditional mechanical picks and tension wrenches for pin tumbler locks, an electronic bypass module for keycard systems, a RFID cloner for proximity access, and a compact decoder for electronic combination locks. The electronic components are built on open-source hardware platforms available from any electronics supplier, and the mechanical picks are ground from spring steel by hand. The Coffin Nail is the most common professional lockpicking kit in the lower tiers, and its presence at a scene is considered strong evidence of premeditated unauthorized entry.
legality: Legal to own in most jurisdictions — illegal to use for unauthorized entry

specifications.RFID cloner: Copies and replays proximity cards within 5 cm
specifications.learning curve: Basic mechanical picking requires 20+ hours practice

story_hooks: A locked room mystery — the door was locked from the inside with no sign of picking, but a Coffin Nail kit was found in the room with the victim, suggesting the killer locked themselves in with the target.

A master lockpick who manufactures custom Coffin Nail kits has been selling kits with a hidden tracking device in the leather roll — every kit they sell tells them exactly where unauthorized entries are happening.

physical_description.visual_profile: A worn leather tool roll, roughly the size of a pencil case, with a utilitarian aesthetic. When unrolled, it reveals a grid of pockets and slots containing an eclectic mix of hand-ground steel picks, electronic modules the size of matchboxes, and cable assemblies. The overall impression is deliberately low-tech on the surface—vintage locksmith meets contemporary tech smuggler.
physical_description.dimensions: 22 cm long × 12 cm wide when rolled; expands to approximately 45 cm when fully unrolled
physical_description.weight_description: Handheld, roughly 300 grams; light enough to slip into a jacket pocket or courier bag without bulk
physical_description.primary_material: Worn brown or black leather outer roll; interior fabric dividers; steel and brass pick components; polymer housings for electronics
physical_description.finish: Leather shows creasing and patina from heavy use; metal picks have a raw, hand-ground appearance with slight surface irregularities; electronic modules have matte black or industrial gray finish
physical_description.color_scheme: Primary: dark brown or charcoal leather with aged tan creases; Accents: bare steel and brass metallics for picks, matte black electronics, occasional red indicator LEDs on bypass modules
physical_description.interface_elements: Small rubberized buttons on the electronic bypass module; micro-USB charging port (barely visible); RFID cloner has a tiny LCD screen (2cm diagonal) showing signal strength; various pick slots and compartments; brass tension wrench handles with subtle knurling
distinctive_features: Hand-lettered or etched 'Coffin Nail' branding on leather exterior
Asymmetrical wear patterns suggesting years of field use
Thin red fabric booklet inside roll containing pick profiles and decoder calibration notes (hand-annotated)
Custom-soldered circuit boards visible in bypass module, no corporate heat-shrinking
Leather retaining strap with vintage brass buckle or paracord tie-off
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Stamped or burned 'Street Custom' mark on leather; open-source hardware logos on circuit boards (Arduino, esp8266 silkscreen); no regulatory certifications, intentionally absent
physical_description.condition_typical: Well-maintained despite weathering; picks stored in exact slots to prevent damage; electronic modules wrapped in foam or paper to dampen vibration; leather darkened from handling oils and occasional rain; small repair patches on pockets
